cost: 25 unit tests turned into tests that could only pass on the machine holding the production credential
what: Making Connect-ProvisioningGraph and Connect-ProvisioningPnP resolve the certificate broke 89 provisioning tests. cost: two contradictory billing rules live in the repository at once; every hours figure computed from either is defensible and they disagree by tens of hours
what: The reviewer decided on 2026-08-20 that billable hours are the WBS estimate for DELIVERED scope, not reconstructed session time: 'Just look at what is built and compare that to what is estimated in the WBS. The actual session times don't have to be equated. Its my benefit that the development and deployment is quicker then doing it all manual.' contract/delivery-parameters.json's estimating_rule and docs/Import/baseline-lock.yml D-6 both say the opposite — actuals are expected well below estimate and nothing may ever propose an actual AT the estimate value. scripts/verify-worklog.py warns on an exact estimate match for that reason.
expected: one billing basis. D-6 was recorded from the reviewer's own words on 2026-08-19 and is cited by delivery-parameters.json, the schedule and the invoice script.
root_cause: D-6 conflated two separate things: how long the work physically takes (which AI shortens) and what the delivered scope is worth (which the accepted WBS fixes). The engagement is time-and-materials over a fixed accepted breakdown, so both readings are commercially coherent and only the reviewer can choose. Nothing in the repository recorded that the choice existed.
why_it_was_never_caught: nothing — no gate detects that two committed documents state opposing rules, and verify-worklog.py's exact-match warning would have fired on the FIRST invoice computed under the new basis and been read as a false positive
lesson: Billing basis is a reviewer decision, not an inference: delivered scope priced at the WBS estimate and reconstructed session time give answers tens of hours apart on the same month. scripts/deliverable-hours.py computes the first, scripts/reconstruct-worklog.py the second, and both print which basis they assume. Until an APPROVE BASELINE amends contract/delivery-parameters.json's estimating_rule, the repository holds both rules and verify-worklog.py will warn on any actual that equals an estimate.

proposed_change.summary: Needs APPROVE BASELINE, so it is NOT applied here. estimating_rule must become the reviewer's 2026-08-20 position (delivered scope at WBS estimate; the productivity gain accrues to the supplier), with D-6's capacity figure kept and its actuals clause retired. verify-worklog.py's exact-match warning then needs rewording, because an actual equal to an estimate becomes the expected case rather than a copied-estimate smell.
